 All tech eyes on Grand Theft Auto VI release Thursday

 Buffalo, N.Y. (WBEN) - Later this week will see the official release of one of the most anticipated video games in recent memory - Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI).
 Ahead of Thursday's release, major tech companies Sony and Microsoft - the parent companies for PlayStation and Xbox, respectively - have already crowned GTA VI their most pre-ordered video game in their digital stores' history. As of late last week, it was estimated that more than 11 million units had already been sold, with pre-sale numbers eclipsing the $1 billion mark.
 Just for context, the last GTA franchise game released in 2013 - GTA V - sold 230 million copies.
 Local cybersecurity expert Arun Vishwanath estimates the engagement with the game is going to be intense off the bat, with people spending weeks and months playing the game. 
 With its highly anticipated release Thursday, Vishwanath says t he question isn't whether this game will break the internet.
 "The bigger question is, 'How will the digital infrastructure handle that many people downloading it all at the same time?' I think that's what it's coming down to at the end of the day, and it's a wait and watch [approach]," said Vishwanath in an interview with WBEN. "I think even though you preloaded it, I think the real game comes live on Nov. 19. So it's going to be a really interesting thing to wait and watch. Hopefully, we don't have another major shortage of something going on in the back end."
 While the pre-loading process for the game has already slowed down the internet a bit, Vishwanath will be watching how much that will be affected once the game is released fully on Thursday. 
 "Are we going to see a slowdown? I doubt it. I think we're ready for it," he said. "I know of many of the infrastructure providers, the backbone out there who already has the capacity built into it - locally, regionally, nationally, and internationally to some extent. I don't expect anything major to go down, but I do expect pockets of issues that we're going to see in some parts." 
 Vishwanath certainly understands the excitement around the release of this game after years of development within its parent company Rockstar Games. He says much has changed with technology and development of games since the last version of Grand Theft Auto came out. 
 "In technology, a month is like a year; so a decade, you're talking about 25-50 years of development happening, both in terms of capacity and all the tech that we have," Vishwanath explained. " Back in the day, even a decade ago, games were not prime-time. This is a big deal. This is a cultural phenomenon, if you ask me. So just in terms of the expectations of what we expect from games have changed the amount of immersion, the engagement, the quality of gameplay. And let's not forget, the newer consoles, they're just capable of running so much more. So the expectations, the time it's taken to build these game worlds itself, they have expanded dramatically because I think the audience expectations have gone up." 
 From a cybersecurity standpoint, Vishwanath knows there's opportunities for cyber criminals out there to take advantage, especially with what has already been revealed for GTA VI. 
 "Having - just like Microsoft - one dominant product out there, it also makes it easier for the bad guys out there to try to hack into it," he warned. "Don't forget, Rockstar got hacked in 2022 when the game was still in development, and there was a social engineering attack where there was a release of early visuals of GTA VI. Again, because of the value of these kind of products, the bad guys out there, the hackers out there target both the gamers as well as these companies. So we're seeing that." 
 So what's Vishwanath's best advice in order to avoid the possibility of falling victim to one of these cyber criminals? 
 "Don't go out there looking for an early deal on something, because it doesn't exist. If it's too good to be true, it's probably not. It's probably a fake," Vishwanath said. "And there are no early releases available for anyone out there, no matter what you pay for it or how little you pay for it. Wait for the official download, and if there's a downtime and it's taking time to load, wait it out rather than trying to look for a workaround." 
 He adds the safest conduits today to get the best quality version of the game are the official app stores - Sony for PlayStation and Microsoft for Xbox. 
 "That, to me, is the best way to deal with this," Vishwanath added. "Thankfully, in the last decade, it's become better. The app markets have become better, they've become more formalized. So we have official channels to get this. Wait for the official channel." 
 "We have the infrastructure for it, but will it be able to handle this when it's happening simultaneously globally, all at the same time?" - Arun Vishwanath
